title: Historical archive
lede: Photographs, advertisements, clippings, and printed maps from Neville Island, the P&OV and PC&Y, and the Pittsburgh river valleys. Credits link to the original wherever it could be found.

items.title: “New Products from Pittsburgh’s Isle of Chemicals”
items.caption: Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical Co. advertisement showing the Neville Island plant from the air and three new units: pipe-line enamel, agricultural chemicals, and phthalic anhydride.
items.credit: Industrial & Engineering Chemistry 41(5), p. 75A (American Chemical Society)
items.rights: Trade-journal advertisement; ACS hosts the page image.

items.title: “Pittsburgh … a dependable source for coal chemicals”
items.caption: Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical Co. Chemical Sales Division advertisement listing Neville Island products: benzol, toluol, tar bases, sulphate of ammonia, pig iron, Neville coke, and cement.
items.credit: Industrial & Engineering Chemistry 39(12), p. 40A (American Chemical Society)
items.rights: Trade-journal advertisement; ACS hosts the page image.

items.title: USS Chemicals Neville Island Plant: “Proud of Our Progress”
items.caption: Full-page advertisement tracing the plant's lineage: Davison Coke & Iron (1928), Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical (1944), and USS Chemicals, a division of U.S. Steel (from 1964). Page 59 of an unidentified Coraopolis-area community booklet.
items.credit: Unidentified booklet, p. 59; via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

items.title: Pittsburgh, Chartiers & Youghiogheny Railway, by Ivan W. Saunders
items.caption: First page of a short PC&Y history: chartered 26 October 1881, built McKees Rocks–Beechmont 1882–83, and joined to the Neville Island Branch over the back-channel bridge, the only rail entrance to the island it shared with the P&OV.
items.credit: Ivan W. Saunders, p. 159; page scan via JSTOR
items.rights: Journal article; check JSTOR terms before reuse.

items.title: P&OV Locomotive 4 at the Monongahela Railroad shop
items.caption: Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway No. 4 at the Monongahela Railroad locomotive repair shop. The P&OV served the steel and coke plants on Neville Island and shut down in the 1990s.
items.credit: Ken Kobus. Ken Kobus Photograph Collection, AIS.2006.18, Archives & Special Collections, University of Pittsburgh Library System
items.rights: In Copyright (rights statement on the ULS record).

items.title: P&OV SW8 at Neville Island, 1978
items.caption: Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley SW8 switching beside a plant building on Neville Island. The caption on the print reads “P&OV SW8, Neville Island PA, 1978, Joe DeFranco.”
items.credit: Joe DeFranco (caption on photo); via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

items.title: P&LE District stations and connections
items.caption: Station list for the Lake Erie R.R. on the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie District, Aliquippa to McKees Rocks. Lists P&OV Jct. (70059) and Neville Island (78002, connections PCY and POV).
items.credit: Unidentified station list; via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

items.title: P&OV scale ticket, Form SJ2047
items.caption: Blank Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Co. weigh ticket: car initial and number, gross, tare and net, contents, from/to, weather, and the weigher's name.
items.credit: Via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

items.title: “To Be Weighed” scale manifest: asphalt to Neville Island, 1967
items.caption: Scale manifest for car ROG 79674 shipped from Bendersville, Pa., to Neville Island, Pa., with asphalt, waybill 161 dated 7/26/67, and weighed at Carl[e], Pa.
items.credit: eBay listing (seller not recorded)
items.rights: Listing photo; seller owns the item.

items.title: Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical to double pig iron (NYT, 1951)
items.caption: Financial page item on PC&C's rights offering to fund a second Neville Island blast furnace, raising output from 300,000 to 600,000 net tons a year.
items.credit: The New York Times, 6 July 1951, p. 26
items.rights: Newspaper page; see the Articles page for the transcription.

items.title: End of Neville Island and Davis Island from the air
items.caption: Early aerial view of the upper end of Neville Island with its plants, the back-channel bridge, and the rail yards on the mainland. A hand-lettered caption reads “End of Neville Island & Davis Island.”

items.title: J. B. Higbee Glass Factory, Bridgeville
items.caption: Postcard view of the Higbee glass works in Kirwan Heights, Bridgeville, on the Chartiers Valley line. General Electric later bought the plant for bulb glass.
items.credit: © Bridgeville Area Historical Society (watermark on image)
items.rights: Watermarked by the Society; ask before reuse.

items.title: Flannery Bolt Co.: “From the Pacific to the Atlantic”
items.caption: Two-page Railway Age advertisement for Flannery hollow flexible staybolts, made in Bridgeville, Pa., on the Chartiers Valley line.
items.credit: Railway Age, 16 November 1940; scan from martynbane.co.uk

items.title: Flannery Bolt Co.: staybolts for the B&O 2-8-8-4s
items.caption: Railway Age advertisement: “Hollow Flexible Staybolts on the 20 new 2-8-8-4s for the Baltimore and Ohio — and now ten more on order” (B&O EM-1 class).
items.credit: Railway Age (page footer); copy from a Facebook post

items.title: Flannery Bolt Co.: F.B.C. universal welded flexible staybolts
items.caption: The Boiler Maker advertisement for Flannery Bolt Company, then at 3528 Forbes Street, Pittsburgh.
items.credit: The Boiler Maker, December 1923 (tear sheet); eBay listing photo
items.rights: Pre-1930 US publication: likely public domain.

items.title: Streetcar signed NEVILLE ISLAND
items.caption: Streetcar No. 9x signed NEVILLE ISLAND, on street track under the trolley wire.
items.credit: eBay listing photo (photographer unknown)

items.title: PRR “OB” interlocking, Becks Run, Pa.
items.caption: Pennsylvania Railroad Monongahela Division track and signal diagram for OB interlocking at Becks Run, a 35-lever electro-pneumatic machine also controlling the Scully lines. Plan last corrected 1-18-46.
items.credit: Pennsylvania Railroad; via North American Interlockings

items.title: P&LE Becks Run tower with a freight, 1984

items.title: “P. & L. E. Rebuilds Interlocking” (1951)
items.caption: Railway Signaling and Communications article on the new all-relay CH interlocking at McKees Rocks, the gateway to the P&LE yards, PC&Y, and Neville Island.

items.title: Pittsburgh & West Virginia Time Table No. 27 (1956)

items.title: “This is Shenango!” company booklet
items.caption: Cover of the Shenango company booklet, showing the lake freighter William P. Snyder Jr. Shenango later owned the Neville Island coke works.
